# Automatic bottom column-chart legends

Original controls generated by `tools/column_chart_legends_fixture.py` from the
original chart-title OPC shell. The reference application exported the retained
PDFs with the sources opened read-only. `tools/record_column_chart_legends.py`
records source/PDF hashes, plot bounds, label baselines and every colored legend
key. No corpus artwork or external document engine is included.

Twenty-one controls vary Arial 6/9/18pt, Calibri 11pt, frame width, label length,
one/two/three rows, stacked versus clustered data, clustered-axis headroom, seven chart heights and larger value-axis fonts.
For this automatic layout subset, entry widths combine measured text advances
with 0.9 face heights; desired single-row width adds 20% spacing, capped at 90%
of the chart width. Entries share the remaining single-row space. Multi-row
legends use equal-width columns, and a one-column stacked legend reverses series
order. Legend keys and vertical placement use face metrics. The legend reserves
its height plus 6pt below the normal category-label band. The code's spacing
constants are reference consumer behavior established by controls, not normative
OOXML dimensions.

The clustered controls expose a pre-existing axis boundary error. The reference application leaves
5% positive-range headroom: maximum 10 uses an axis ending at 12, 9.4 ends at 10,
and 9.6 ends at 12. With the 288pt frame, 9.4 uses a 1-unit step, while the
other two use a 2-unit step. Height probes place the 9pt-font density transition
between 186pt and 192pt frames. Automatic positive clustered tick counts use
plot height divided by 1.1 face heights, capped at ten intervals, before rounding
the headroom-adjusted range to a 1/2/5 tick step. Large axis fonts also require
extra space between the title and plot. Percent-stacked scaling is unchanged.

Browser tests compare plot geometry, key rectangles and available PDF label
origins/baselines within 0.2pt. Pypdf loses some successive label origins in these
PDF streams; all legend key positions are independently checked using PDFium.
Tests also cover editing, exact undo, untouched ZIP parts and export/reopen.
Manual/overlaid legends, deletion overrides, decorated text and left/top legends
remain outside this extension. These controls do not establish clipping or
wrapping within an individual label wider than the available legend width.
